findings.claim: The waivers-path existence check at policy-check.yml lines 273-276 is dead code. scripts/verify-bypass-pairing.sh exits 1 at line 39 when the waivers file is absent, so if the script returned 0 the file is guaranteed present. The outer `[ ! -f ]` guard is unreachable.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml line 268: `PAIRING_METADATA="$(... scripts/verify-bypass-pairing.sh ...)" || { emit_error ...; exit 1; }` catches all non-zero exits. Lines 273-276: `if [ ! -f "${SCP_WAIVERS_PATH}" ]; then emit_error SCP-E004 ...; exit 1; fi` executes only after a clean script return. scripts/verify-bypass-pairing.sh line 39: `if [ ! -f "${waivers_path}" ]; then echo ... >&2; exit 1; fi` — absent file is already caught by the script. Flagged C-nit-02 in R1 consolidation; carried open per fixpoint semantics (nit-only items not required for closure).
findings.impact: No runtime impact. Future maintainers may incorrectly treat the outer check as meaningful defence-in-depth when it is structurally unreachable, leading to false confidence if the script's internal check is ever refactored away.
findings.mitigation: Remove lines 273-276 from the bypass-gate step, leaving verify-bypass-pairing.sh as the sole waivers-existence guard. If defence-in-depth is desired, add a comment instead of a redundant code path.

findings.claim: The SCP-E004 workflow log annotation at policy-check.yml line 327 uses raw `${expires_at}` (user-provided, may be date-only, e.g. `2026-06-01`), while the structured `bypass_record.waiver_expires_at` in the summary artifact uses the normalized RFC3339 value `${waiver_expires_at}` (e.g. `2026-06-01T00:00:00Z`). An operator correlating the workflow log to the artifact will see two different expiry representations for the same bypass event.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml line 327: `printf '::error file=%s,title=SCP-E004::break-glass bypass active for %s via %s until %s\n' "${SCP_WAIVERS_PATH}" "${BYPASS_RULE_ID}" "${decision_id:-D-unknown}" "${expires_at}"` — raw value. Lines 324-325: `append_github_env_multiline "SCP_BYPASS_EXPIRES_AT" "${waiver_expires_at}"` — normalized RFC3339 written to GITHUB_ENV. policy-check.yml line 481: `"waiver_expires_at": os.environ.get("SCP_BYPASS_EXPIRES_AT", "")` — artifact reads normalized value. Carried from R3 review as nit-R3-BYPASS-001.
findings.impact: No security impact. Bypass gate correctness, schema validation, and audit artifact integrity are all unaffected. Risk is limited to operator confusion when correlating log events with artifact records (e.g. in a post-incident review where a date-only log entry and a full datetime artifact record must be matched by hand).
findings.mitigation: Change line 327 to reference `${waiver_expires_at}` instead of `${expires_at}` so the human-readable annotation and the structured artifact record both show the same normalized RFC3339 timestamp.

findings.claim: The `waivers-path` workflow input is stripped of a leading `./` (script line 13) but is not canonicalized against `../` traversal. A calling workflow could set `waivers-path` to a path that resolves outside the repository workspace (e.g. `../../runner/_work/tmp/attacker-crafted.json`). The script would accept the path if the target file exists and passes schema validation.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-bypass-pairing.sh line 13: `waivers_path="${waivers_path#./}"` — strips one level of `./` prefix only. Line 39: `[ ! -f "${waivers_path}" ]` — existence check; any resolvable path passes. Line 52-58: `jq ... "${waivers_path}"` — jq reads the file. policy-check.yml line 278-302: Python schema validation runs on the file — if the target file happens to be valid waivers JSON satisfying the schema, validation passes. No realpath or workspace-boundary check is applied at any layer. DECISIONS.md rows are hardcoded to `docs/DECISIONS.md`; only the waivers path is caller-supplied.
findings.impact: In practice the attack surface is minimal: the calling workflow is repo-owner-controlled code subject to its own review and branch protection; the runner filesystem is ephemeral; and a non-JSON path causes jq to fail with exit 1 (gate rejects, not bypasses). A determined hostile workflow author already has easier attack vectors (they could rewrite the calling workflow itself). A careless developer pointing to a wrong path will see a gate failure rather than a silent bypass. This is a defence-in-depth gap, not an exploitable bypass in the standard CI threat model.
findings.mitigation: Add `waivers_path="$(realpath --relative-base="$(pwd)" "${waivers_path}" 2>/dev/null || echo '')"` followed by a guard `[[ "${waivers_path}" == /* ]] && { echo 'waivers-path must be relative to workspace' >&2; exit 1; }` to reject absolute or traversing paths before any file operations. Alternatively, validate that the resolved path is a descendant of `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`.

self_reported_concerns: R3 regex closure verified independently: DECISIONS.md lines 14-40 show all rows use exactly 3-digit D-NNN (D-001 through D-028). The regex `^\+\|\s*D-[0-9]{3}\s*\|\s*20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\s*\|` on line 33 anchors the scan correctly; `grep -oE 'D-[0-9]{3}'` on line 105 extracts it consistently. The schema pattern `^D-[0-9]{3}$` in policy-check-summary.schema.json aligns. No mismatch remains.

MAJ-R2-BYPASS-001 re-confirmed: two independent defences — (1) Python control-char check at policy-check.yml lines 257-265 rejects rule_id containing `\n`, `\r`, or `\x00` before script invocation; (2) `append_github_env_multiline` (lines 309-319) writes all bypass vars via uuidgen-delimited heredoc, immune to content injection regardless of value. Both layers independently sufficient; together provide defence-in-depth appropriate for a break-glass gate.

MAJ-R2-BYPASS-002 re-confirmed: `bypass_record` required by allOf if/then in schema lines 236-253 when `bypass_emitted=true`. Build summary step lines 484-487 additionally validates all four required fields are non-empty before writing. Schema round-trip test at dispatch layer confirmed exit_code=0 for valid case and exit_code=1 for missing bypass_record case.

MIN-R2-BYPASS-003 re-confirmed closed: verify-bypass-pairing.sh line 85 uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()` for date-only expiry comparison, consistent with the datetime-path UTC handling at line 80. No drift surface remains.

bypass_record.decision_id: script line 105 `grep -oE 'D-[0-9]{3}'` can only extract a 3-digit D-NNN because decision_row was already constrained by the anchored regex on line 33 to contain `\s*D-[0-9]{3}\s*`. If decision_row is non-empty, decision_id is guaranteed non-empty and matches `^D-[0-9]{3}$`. No empty-string bypass path.

Conftest supply-chain: still lacks `gh attestation verify` (Sigstore). Acknowledged at workflow line 158. Carried residual from R1. Outside the break-glass bypass attack surface. Not a new finding at R4.

uuidgen dependency: ubuntu-24.04 GitHub-hosted runners include uuidgen (util-linux package). Absence causes command substitution failure under `set -euo pipefail`, producing an infra failure (SCP-E001 class) rather than a silent bypass. Not a bypass vector.

The extraction grep on line 105 also uses `D-[0-9]{3}`, which is consistent with the schema pattern `^D-[0-9]{3}$` in policy-check-summary.schema.json. No regression was introduced by the fix. Both R2 MAJ closures (MAJ-R2-BYPASS-001: GITHUB_ENV injection; MAJ-R2-BYPASS-002: bypass_emitted without structured record) and the R2 MIN closure (MIN-R2-BYPASS-003: date.today() UTC drift) hold under independent re-examination. Fresh R4 attack surface yields no new CRIT or MAJ. Three nit-level findings carry forward or are newly raised: nit-R2-BYPASS-004 (dead-code waivers-existence check, expected-open), nit-R3-BYPASS-001 (log annotation vs artifact expiry format inconsistency, carried from R3), and nit-R4-BYPASS-001 (caller-supplied waivers-path lacks `../` canonicalization guard). All three are cosmetic or defence-in-depth improvements; none enable a bypass. Fixpoint: APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS (nit-only).
